articles.title: US Moves to Strip Citizenship From 40 People in Largest Denaturalization Push Yet
articles.excerpt: The Justice Department filed 40 denaturalization cases between Aug. 21 and Oct. 2 against naturalized citizens accused of serious crimes and immigration fraud — the biggest such push in modern US history.
articles.image_caption: A U.S. passport. The government has moved to strip citizenship from 40 people in the largest denaturalization drive in decades.
articles.nri_angle: One Indian national is named among the 40 denaturalization targets, and the sweeping push puts the large Indian naturalized population and N-400 applicants on notice that concealment on immigration forms — however old — can now trigger loss of citizenship.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Radiology Groups Join Coalition Against $103,265 H-1B Fee on Physicians
articles.excerpt: The American College of Radiology and dozens of physician and patient advocacy groups told federal immigration officials the proposed fee would make it harder to recruit doctors for rural and underserved communities.
articles.image_caption: An MRI scanner in a hospital radiology suite. Radiology groups are urging the Trump administration to exempt physicians from the new $100,000 H-1B fee.
articles.nri_angle: The fee would hit hardest at safety-net hospitals and rural practices that rely on international medical graduates, a workforce that includes many Indian-trained physicians working in the US on H-1B status.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: September's Global Immigration Shifts: What Changed for Visa Seekers Worldwide
articles.excerpt: From Australia's new skilled-visa priority rules to Japan's twentyfold permanent residence fee hike and a UK settlement overhaul on the horizon, September brought rule changes that directly affect Indian migrants.
articles.image_caption: WR Immigration's September 2026 global immigration recap graphic. The recap covers rule changes in Canada, Australia, the United Kingdom, Japan, Saudi Arabia, New Zealand, and Thailand.
articles.nri_angle: Australia's onshore-first processing favors Indian students and graduates already in the country, while the UK's coming earned-settlement overhaul could reshape ILR eligibility for thousands of Indians nearing five years of residence.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Montana Governor Lands in India to Rescue Lentil Exports Amid MAGA Backlash
articles.excerpt: Governor Greg Gianforte is leading a 30-member delegation to India and Sri Lanka to rebuild the state's collapsed pulse trade, even as anti-India voices in his own party attack the trip.
articles.image_caption: Montana Governor Greg Gianforte. He is leading a 30-plus member delegation to India and Sri Lanka, with reviving Montana's lentil exports to India the centerpiece of the trip.
articles.nri_angle: The trip exposes a paradox for Indian Americans: anti-India voices demand the governor's impeachment while Montana's farm economy and universities actively court Indian consumers, students, and research ties.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Extends $100K H-1B Fee to 2027 Even as Courts Block Collection
articles.excerpt: The Sept. 18 extension keeps the $100,000 H-1B payment alive through Sept. 2027 — but two federal judges have barred agencies from collecting it while the administration's appeal plays out.
articles.image_caption: A close-up of a U.S. visa foil showing the H-1B visa type. The Trump administration extended the $100,000 payment on new overseas H-1B petitions through Sept. 2027, though federal courts have barred its collection.
articles.nri_angle: Indians receive roughly three-quarters of H-1B visas, so the $100,000 fee on new overseas hires would land hardest on Indian tech workers — for now the courts have kept it off the books, but the legal limbo is delaying adjudications.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump H-1B Fee Fight Heads to a Showdown Over Congress's Authority
articles.excerpt: Judges in Massachusetts and California have ruled the $100,000 fee amounts to a tax only Congress can impose; the administration has responded with a new $103,265 rulemaking that 22 states oppose.
articles.image_caption: US President Donald Trump; courts have ruled his administration's 00,000 H-1B fee amounts to an unauthorized tax on Congress's taxing power
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals are the largest H-1B beneficiaries; the fee effectively froze skilled hiring at hospitals, universities and schools — no fee is collectible today, but the $103,265 rulemaking means the question is dormant, not dead.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mother of US Green Card Holder Denied Visitor Visa: 214(b) Rules and Interview Tips
articles.excerpt: A Green Card holder's mother was refused a B1/B2 visitor visa within minutes at the Mumbai consulate despite showing savings, property and investments. Reddit users - and the 214(b) rule itself - say it was never about money at all.
articles.image_caption: The US Embassy in New Delhi. The mother of a US green card holder was denied a visitor visa under Section 214(b).
articles.nri_angle: Green Card holders and US citizens inviting parents over must build the case around the parent's roots in India - steady income, property, a short specific itinerary - because a 214(b) denial has no appeal, only a stronger reapplication.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New Decade-Long Study Finds H-1B Workers Paid 15% Less Than Peers
articles.excerpt: Harvard economist George Borjas's analysis of 2014–2024 records finds visa holders better educated but underpaid — though critics say the wage gap is far smaller than claimed.
articles.image_caption: H-1B visa workers, who a decade-long study found are paid 15% less than their peers
articles.nri_angle: The wage-gap debate bears directly on Indian professionals, the largest group of H-1B beneficiaries, as the fate of the $100,000 fee will shape U.S. employer sponsorship in coming years.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DACA and TPS Holders Face Tougher Travel Rules After Immigration Appeals Board Ruling
articles.excerpt: The August decision overturns a 12-year-old rule — advance parole trips can now trigger three- or 10-year bars on reentry to the United States.
articles.image_caption: Supporters at a DACA rally. A Board of Immigration Appeals ruling means DACA and TPS holders who leave the US could trigger reentry bars.
articles.nri_angle: Indian DACA recipients and adjustment-of-status applicants lose a once-safe travel option, raising the stakes of every family visit home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Russia to Take 70,000 Indian Skilled Workers This Year, Jaishankar Tells Parliament Panel
articles.excerpt: The external affairs minister's briefing covered trade, energy and Ukraine diplomacy — plus India's push to bring home citizens recruited into Russia's military.
articles.image_caption: S. Jaishankar, India's External Affairs Minister, who told Parliament that Russia will take 70,000 Indian skilled workers this year.
articles.nri_angle: The 70,000-worker commitment opens a major new overseas employment channel for Indians, alongside the government's effort to repatriate those fraudulently recruited into Russia's military.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Visa Application Mistakes First-Time Travelers Must Avoid
articles.excerpt: Most visa refusals for first-time travelers come down to avoidable errors — mismatched documents, weak financial proof, vague itineraries, passport validity and dishonest disclosures. Here's how to get each one right.
articles.image_caption: An Indian passport — documentation errors are the top driver of visa rejections for first-time travellers
articles.nri_angle: First-time Indian travelers most often need visas for the diaspora's core routes — the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf — so these documentation rules are the practical gateway to visiting family abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Exempt From $20,000 US Visa Bond Rule as 50 Countries Listed
articles.excerpt: The US State Department has finalized a permanent visa-bond program for B1/B2 applicants from 50 countries, with bonds of $10,000 to $20,000 set at consular officers' discretion. Indian passport holders are not on the list.
articles.image_caption: A woman holding an Indian passport speaks with a consular officer at a US visa application window. Indian passport holders are exempt from the new US visa-bond requirement, which covers B1/B2 applicants from 50 listed countries.
articles.nri_angle: Indian passport holders are exempt, but the diaspora should track the list because it covers neighboring countries many Indian-American families receive relatives from.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DHS Moves to End Work Permits for H-1B Spouses, Reviving Trump-Era H-4 EAD Fight
articles.excerpt: The administration has placed H-4 employment-authorization rescission on its regulatory agenda as a long-term action, but no proposed rule has been drafted — current permit holders keep their authorization for now.
articles.nri_angle: The rule's impact would fall hardest on Indian families, who account for the bulk of H-4 EAD holders and face decades-long green card waits.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: JD Vance Backs Scrapping H-1B Visa Programme, Calling It 'Completely Broken'
articles.excerpt: The vice president defended the administration's blocked $100,000 H-1B fee while a second federal judge halted its enforcement, escalating a fight that weighs heavily on Indian professionals.
articles.image_caption: US Vice President JD Vance speaks at a microphone in front of an American flag, in a composite news graphic. Vance said on October 1 that he would support eliminating the H-1B visa programme, which he called ‘completely broken.’
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals, who make up a large share of H-1B holders, face the deepest uncertainty as the courts, the White House and Congress pull the programme in different directions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Australia Tightens Student Transfer Rules: 12-Month Wait Now Required to Switch Providers
articles.excerpt: The temporary change, effective 2 October 2026, doubles the previous six-month restriction and can catch students already studying in Australia — with the clock reset for some.
articles.image_caption: A university campus in Australia; new rules require international students to wait 12 months before transferring institutions.
articles.nri_angle: Indian students, among the largest cohorts in Australian international education, must factor the new transfer rules into enrolment decisions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'Passportmaxxing': H-1B Uncertainty Pushes Indians in US Toward Second Residencies
articles.excerpt: A Dubai-based citizenship advisory firm says it has processed 450+ Indian clients for second passports as green-card backlogs and tougher visa enforcement turn mobility into an asset class.
articles.image_caption: Indian professionals in the US are increasingly buying second residencies and citizenships as a Plan B against H-1B and green-card uncertainty.
articles.nri_angle: H-1B families are pricing the risk of employer-sponsored status and buying residency optionality — with the caveat that India bars dual citizenship.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Second US Judge Blocks Trump's $100,000 H-1B Fee in Oakland Ruling
articles.excerpt: Judge Haywood Gilliam ruled USCIS and the State Department skipped required rulemaking before imposing the fee, granting unions and employers a block while their lawsuit proceeds — the second such defeat after Boston's June ruling.
articles.nri_angle: Indians are the largest H-1B recipients, so a second judicial block on the $100,000 fee directly protects Indian professionals and employers — though the push for a permanent $103,000 fee means uncertainty persists.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Expands Social Media Screening to Journalists, TN and TD Visa Applicants
articles.excerpt: Starting October 1, the State Department adds I, TN, and TD visa applicants to its online-presence review — the latest wave of social media vetting that already covers students, H-1B workers, and more.
articles.nri_angle: Indian journalists on I visas are the main Indian group newly affected; the expansion is another step in digital vetting that already covers the student and H-1B visas most Indians use.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: California Bans AI-Only Firing of Workers With Landmark No Robo Bosses Act
articles.excerpt: Governor Gavin Newsom signed SB 947 on September 30, making California the first state to require a human to corroborate any termination or discipline decision driven primarily by AI — reversing his veto of a similar bill last year.
articles.nri_angle: California's large Indian diaspora tech workforce gains a concrete safeguard against opaque automated firing and discipline decisions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
